chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have purchased a camel, so what should I do with it?' He said: 'Go until you reach Masjid Al-Shajara, pour water over yourself, and wear your two garments. Then kneel it facing the Qiblah. Then enter the mosque, pray, then complete your prayer. Then go out to it and mark it from the right side of its hump. Then say: 'In the Name of Allah, O Allah, from You and to You. O Allah, accept from me.' Then go until you reach Al-Bayda', and recite the Talbiyyah.'

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاء: Al-Bayda', a plain near Mecca where pilgrims traditionally recite the Talbiyyah
key_terms.بَدَنَة: A camel used for sacrifice or pilgrimage
key_terms.لَبِّ: To recite the Talbiyyah (the declaration of readiness for pilgrimage)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid Al-Shajara, a specific location near Mecca associated with the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for consecrating a sacrificial camel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual consecration (tamkin) of a sacrificial camel, emphasizing the integration of physical preparation with spiritual devotion through prayer and supplication at Masjid al-Shajara. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking the physical act of marking the animal with the spiritual state of the pilgrim, culminating in the recitation of the Talbiyyah at Al-Bayda', a site historically significant in Islamic pilgrimage narratives.
